caption: Figure 1: Primary near-eye multiplicative associations for seven daily metrics. Points and bars are estimates and pointwise 95% confidence intervals; the reference ratio is one.
alt: Three-panel forest plot of primary near-eye multiplicative daily-metric associations. Seven metric rows per panel show point estimates and pointwise 95 percent confidence intervals around a vertical null ratio of one for Free versus Work day, Active versus Sedentary day, and each additional hour of previous-night sleep.

caption: Figure 2: Primary near-eye absolute associations for six duration or timing metrics. Points and bars are differences in hours and pointwise 95% confidence intervals; the reference difference is zero.
alt: Three-panel forest plot of primary near-eye absolute daily duration and clock-time associations in hours. Six metric rows per panel show point estimates and pointwise 95 percent confidence intervals around a vertical null difference of zero for the three day-level contexts.

caption: Figure 3: FDR decision overview for the primary and gap-timing-unaware daily-metric association families.
alt: Two stacked grids summarize the 15 named daily metrics across the three day-level contexts for the primary and gap-timing-unaware datasets. Filled blue circles mark FDR-supported associations with explicit limitations; open grey circles mark associations without FDR support; orange crosses mark non-estimable L10 mean; magenta diamonds mark the MDER result without FDR support. Primary counts are 10, 6, and 12 supported slots for work/free day, activity status, and previous-night sleep; gap counts are 10, 6, and 13.

caption: Figure 4: Site deviations from the site-average context association.
alt: Ten faceted forest plots show nine site adjustment factors for each globally supported primary predictor-by-site interaction. A factor below 1 means the site's comparison-to-reference ratio is lower than the equal-weight site-average ratio, and a factor above 1 means it is higher. Horizontal bars are pointwise 95% confidence intervals. Of 90 site adjustments, 13 are pointwise below 1, 11 are pointwise above 1, and 66 include 1. Filled points use consistent study-site colors and do not encode significance.

caption: Figure 5: Time-varying near-eye context associations from the exploratory 30-minute GAMM. Curves are ratios for fitted Y plus 0.1 lx; bands are pointwise 95% confidence intervals.
alt: Four-panel time-of-day figure for the primary near-eye 30-minute GAMM. Curves show ratios for fitted melEDI plus 0.1 lx across 48 half-hour midpoints for Free versus Work day, Active versus Sedentary status, one additional hour of within-participant sleep, and one additional hour of between-participant mean sleep. Pointwise 95 percent bands accompany each curve and a horizontal line marks ratio one.
